questions.prompt: Why distinguish an Okta global session policy from an app authentication policy?

options.text: They govern different session and authentication requirements
options.explanation: An acceptable provider session does not mean every app requirement is already satisfied.

options.text: Both define every target application's business roles
options.explanation: Local resource authorization is a separate responsibility.

options.text: The app policy always creates target accounts
options.explanation: Authentication requirements do not perform arbitrary provisioning.

options.text: A global session makes every app policy irrelevant
options.explanation: Application-specific requirements can still apply.

review.heading: Give each policy a specific job

questions.prompt: A user has an acceptable Okta session but an app requires stronger assurance. What may happen?

options.text: The user may need an additional authentication check
options.explanation: The app's requirement can exceed what the existing session satisfies.

options.text: The app must ignore its requirement to preserve SSO
options.explanation: SSO does not waive applicable policy assurance.

options.text: Every additional check proves a software defect
options.explanation: A challenge can be correct enforcement.

options.text: The user's source profile must be deleted first
options.explanation: Profile deletion is unrelated to meeting assurance.

questions.prompt: A prompt seems surprising. What should an analyst identify first?

options.text: The actual policy association, matching context and selected rule
options.explanation: The policy that really processed the attempt matters more than a familiar name.

options.text: Any policy with a similar title
options.explanation: Labels do not establish the selected rule.

options.text: Only the number of app assignments
options.explanation: Assignment count does not identify authentication requirements.

options.text: Always the oldest policy in the org
options.explanation: Age alone does not establish evaluation context.

review.heading: Identify the policy that actually applies

evidence: Policy with familiar name: not confirmed associated
Actual selected rule and evaluated context: not yet supplied

questions.prompt: A browser holds separate provider and app sessions. What should be assumed about their lifetimes?

options.text: Each has its own applicable state and policy
options.explanation: Federation does not merge all systems' session clocks.

options.text: They always expire at the same instant
options.explanation: That equality is not guaranteed.

options.text: The provider's cookie is the app's local cookie
options.explanation: Session cookies belong to their respective service relationships.

options.text: A new app session proves the provider session is new
options.explanation: An existing provider session can support new app entry.

questions.prompt: A local app session has an idle timeout and an absolute maximum. The user stays active. Which limit may still end it?

options.text: The absolute maximum lifetime
options.explanation: Activity can affect idle handling without eliminating an absolute maximum.

options.text: Neither limit can ever affect an active user
options.explanation: A maximum can apply regardless of continued activity.

options.text: Only a new MFA challenge; active sessions have no maximum
options.explanation: A challenge requirement and a session maximum are separate controls. Continued activity does not remove an absolute maximum.

options.text: Only the IdP session timeout, because app sessions inherit its lifetime
options.explanation: An app can enforce its own local session maximum independently of the IdP session.

review.heading: Keep session lifetime and reauthentication separate

questions.prompt: An app requests another authentication check after an interval. Is that always the same as destroying every session?

options.text: No; authentication freshness and session termination are distinct operations
options.explanation: A new proof requirement does not inherently revoke all unrelated sessions.

options.text: Yes; every challenge means all sessions were deleted
options.explanation: That is broader than the supplied authentication requirement.

options.text: Yes; the user must have a new identity record
options.explanation: A fresh authentication event does not imply a new person or account.

options.text: No policy or event evidence is needed
options.explanation: The applicable rule and actual outcome still need verification.

review.heading: Keep session lifetime and reauthentication separate

questions.prompt: An app ends its own session while Okta remains acceptable. What can a later visit do?

options.text: Start a new sign-in and create a replacement app session
options.explanation: Rapid return can reflect provider reuse rather than survival of the old local session.

options.text: Prove the old app session was never terminated
options.explanation: A new session can explain the observed access.

options.text: Necessarily sign out every other app
options.explanation: Local termination does not establish cross-app scope.

options.text: Skip all app validation forever
options.explanation: A new exchange still requires the receiving app's checks.

review.heading: Define what signing out must accomplish

questions.prompt: A shared authentication policy is changed for one app ticket. What should be assessed?

options.text: Other app associations, matching users and affected requirements
options.explanation: A shared policy change can affect more than the app currently being inspected.

options.text: Only whether the requester gets fewer prompts
options.explanation: That does not assess unintended weakening or wider impact.

options.text: Only whether the rule saves
options.explanation: Save success is not evidence of intended policy outcomes.

options.text: No assessment if the policy name includes the app
options.explanation: The actual associations matter more than its label.

review.heading: Predict who a rule change will affect

evidence: Policy P is associated with Expense and App B
Proposed edit changes P authentication conditions
Impact on App B and its users: not yet tested

questions.prompt: The selected rule requires a new check and the user is prompted accordingly. What is the first interpretation?

options.text: The prompt may be the intended policy outcome
options.explanation: Compare the observed challenge with the approved rule before calling it a defect.

options.text: Every prompt must be removed for SSO to work
options.explanation: Single sign-on can coexist with additional requirements.

options.text: A prompt proves a target account is missing
options.explanation: Account readiness and authentication challenge are different boundaries.

options.text: Every policy must be reset to default
options.explanation: That broad change is not justified by the supplied behavior.

questions.prompt: A policy test predicts no challenge, but no real controlled attempt is recorded. What remains unknown?

options.text: Whether the intended runtime context actually followed that path
options.explanation: A prediction or configuration view is not a verified execution result.

options.text: Whether a prediction was supplied
options.explanation: That limited planning fact is stated directly.

options.text: Whether every user has identical session state
options.explanation: Different users can have different relevant context.

options.text: Whether a successful sign-in would establish all resource permissions
options.explanation: Authentication alone would not establish every local permission.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

questions.prompt: A business request says sign out everywhere. What must be clarified?

options.text: Which systems, sessions and devices are included and how termination is verified
options.explanation: A broad phrase needs supported mechanisms and testable scope.

options.text: Only the text on the local logout button
options.explanation: A label cannot establish cross-system termination.

options.text: An assumption that every SAML app participates automatically
options.explanation: Integration support and configured participation must be checked.

options.text: A rule to permanently delete every user record
options.explanation: Logout and account deletion have different meanings.

review.heading: Define what signing out must accomplish

questions.prompt: Which evidence best explains an app authentication outcome?

options.text: The relevant app association, selected rule, context, authentication result and downstream outcome
options.explanation: These connect intended requirements to a particular observed attempt.

options.text: Only a screenshot of a similarly named policy
options.explanation: That does not establish actual rule selection.

options.text: Only last month's successful login by another user
options.explanation: Different state and context cannot prove this outcome.

options.text: Only an enrollment list
options.explanation: Readiness for a method is not the current policy evaluation result.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

questions.topic: Challenge: A higher rule changes the diagnosis
questions.prompt: An administrator expects a permissive app rule to apply, but the correlated attempt selects a higher-priority restrictive rule. What is established?
evidence: Observed context matches higher-priority rule R1; selected R1 requires a new check
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, state the last confirmed success and the first evidenced gap. What in the packet supports each?

options.text: The observed higher-priority rule selection explains the prompt
options.explanation: A lower rule's presence does not establish selection. Compare actual context and rule order with the approved design before deciding whether the selection is a defect.

options.text: The lower rule must apply because its name mentions this team
options.explanation: A descriptive rule name does not override supplied selection and priority evidence.

options.text: The authenticator enrollment must be corrupt
options.explanation: The packet explains the prompt through policy selection and supplies no enrollment corruption evidence.

options.text: A shared policy cannot have different outcomes for different contexts
options.explanation: Conditional rules exist to distinguish contexts; policy sharing does not imply identical outcomes for every attempt.

review.heading: Identify the policy that actually applies

questions.topic: Challenge: A prompt does not settle session destruction
questions.prompt: A user is challenged again after an authentication interval. Which fact about session state remains unknown from the challenge alone?
evidence: App authentication rule: new check required after the configured interval
Challenge displayed; provider and local app session termination not inspected
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, name the exact missing outcome. Separate it from facts that the packet already supplies.

options.text: Whether either session was terminated rather than requiring reauthentication
options.explanation: Reauthentication and session lifetime are related controls with distinct outcomes. A prompt alone does not establish the destruction of every session.

options.text: Whether another check was requested
options.explanation: The displayed challenge explicitly establishes that narrower observation.

options.text: Whether the supplied rule contains an interval condition
options.explanation: That requirement is supplied; actual session termination is not.

options.text: Whether a challenge was displayed to the user
options.explanation: The packet states that it was. Display and termination are different facts.

review.heading: Keep session lifetime and reauthentication separate

questions.topic: Challenge: A shared rule needs a wider comparison
questions.prompt: A proposed rule edit would remove a prompt in Expense. Which next analysis is most justified before releasing it?
evidence: Rule belongs to Policy P13, shared by Expense and Payroll
Payroll authentication requirement: unchanged; impact of proposed edit not assessed
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, explain which uncertainty your next check would resolve and why the other actions are premature.

options.text: Assess the change against requirements and contexts in both apps
options.explanation: A local symptom can lead to a shared change. Assess Payroll and rule-order effects rather than assuming the Expense outcome is the only consequence.

options.text: Release after testing only the original Expense user
options.explanation: That leaves another explicitly affected app's authentication requirement untested.

options.text: Remove the stronger requirement from both apps for consistency
options.explanation: Consistency is not a substitute for each app's approved requirement.

options.text: Rename the shared policy to Expense Only and keep the same associations
options.explanation: A label does not change the actual app associations or rule behavior.

review.heading: Predict who a rule change will affect

questions.topic: Challenge: Differentiate an old session from a new one
questions.prompt: After local logout, an app opens again without a password prompt. Which evidence best verifies whether logout failed or a new session was created?
evidence: Provider session may remain acceptable; no subsequent request/session trace yet supplied
questions.reasoning: Before selecting, describe the evidence that would show success and the relevant failure or rejection that should remain.

options.text: Correlate old-session invalidation, protected requests and any replacement session
options.explanation: The same user experience can reflect survival or replacement. Correlated old/new state and message flow distinguish the two.

options.text: Conclude failure solely because the next visit had no password prompt
options.explanation: A surviving provider session can support a fresh app session; no prompt does not prove the old local session survived.

options.text: Conclude success solely because the logout button was clicked
options.explanation: The action does not establish that the target invalidated A134.

options.text: Inspect only the provider's configured timeout
options.explanation: Configuration alone does not show the local session outcome or whether a new exchange occurred.

review.heading: Define what signing out must accomplish
